arxiv-1705-00249.title: Unimem: Runtime Data Management on Non-Volatile Memory-based Heterogeneous Main Memory
arxiv-1705-00249.creator: Kai Wu, Yingchao Huang, Dong Li
arxiv-1705-00249.description: Abstract . Non-volatile memory (NVM) provides a scalable and power-efficient solution to replace DRAM as main memory. However, because of relatively high latency and low bandwidth of NVM, NVM is often paired with DRAM to build a heterogeneous memory system (HMS). As a result, data objects of the application must be carefully placed to NVM and DRAM for best performance.

arxiv-1708-00789.title: Complex diffuse emission in the z = 0.52 z=0.52 cluster PLCK G004.5-19.5
arxiv-1708-00789.creator: J. G. Albert, C. Sifón, A. Stroe, F. Mernier, H. T. Intema, H. J. A. Röttgering, G. Brunetti
arxiv-1708-00789.description: Abstract We present radio observations of the galaxy cluster PLCK G004.5-19.5 ( z = 0.52 z=0.52 ) using the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope at 150 MHz, 325 MHz, and 610 MHz. We find an unusual arrangement of diffuse radio emission in the center and periphery of the cluster, as well as several radio galaxies with head-tail emission.

arxiv-2011-13860.title: Nodes on quintic spectrahedra
arxiv-2011-13860.creator: Taylor Brysiewicz, Khazhgali Kozhasov, Mario Kummer
arxiv-2011-13860.description: Abstract We classify transversal quintic spectrahedra by the location of 20 20 nodes on the respective real determinantal surface of degree 5 5 . We identify 65 65 classes of such surfaces and find an explicit representative in each of them. \titlemark Nodes on quintic spectrahedra \MSC Primary: 14J17, 14M12, 14P10, 14Q10, 52A15. Secondary: 14P25, 90C22.

arxiv-2204-01258.creator: Sagnik Sen, Éric Sopena, S Taruni ( a ) (a) Indian Institute of Technology Dharwad, India. ( b ) (b) Université de Bordeaux, LaBRI, France.
arxiv-2204-01258.description: Abstract The study of homomorphisms of ( n , m ) (n,m) -graphs, that is, adjacency preserving vertex mappings of graphs with n n types of arcs and m m types of edges was initiated by Nešetřil and Raspaud [Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B 2000].

arxiv-2405-11465.title: Effective In-Context Example Selection through Data Compression
arxiv-2405-11465.creator: Zhongxiang Sun, Kepu Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Xiao Zhang, Jun XuGaoling School of Artificial Intelligence,Renmin University of China
arxiv-2405-11465.description: Abstract In-context learning has been extensively validated in large language models. However, the mechanism and selection strategy for in-context example selection, which is a crucial ingredient in this approach, lacks systematic and in-depth research. In this paper, we propose a data compression approach to the selection of in-context examples.

arxiv-2408-10445.title: Compression Acceleration of Protons and Heavier Ions at the Heliospheric Current Sheet Journal: ApJ Athena++ ( Stone et al. 2008 ; Jiang et al. 2014 ) , GPAT ( Li et al. 2018b ; Li et al. 2022 )
arxiv-2408-10445.creator: Giulia Murtas, Xiaocan Li, Fan Guo
arxiv-2408-10445.description: Abstract Recent observations by Parker Solar Probe (PSP) suggest that protons and heavier ions are accelerated to high energies by magnetic reconnection at the heliospheric current sheet (HCS). By solving the energetic particle transport equation in large-scale MHD simulations, we study the compression acceleration of protons and heavier ions in the reconnecting HCS.

arxiv-2411-11974.title: A Novel Bispectrum Estimator of the Kinematic Sunyaev-Zel’dovich Effect using Projected Fields
arxiv-2411-11974.creator: Raagini Patki, Nicholas Battaglia, J. Colin Hill
arxiv-2411-11974.description: Abstract With the advent of current and future high-resolution CMB experiments, the kinematic Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (kSZ) effect has become a unique observational probe of the distribution of baryons and velocities in the Universe. In this work, we propose a novel binned bispectrum of the form temperature-temperature-density to extract the late-time kSZ effect from cleaned CMB maps.

arxiv-2504-01851.title: Virtual Target Trajectory Prediction for Stochastic Targets
arxiv-2504-01851.creator: Marc Schneider, Renato Loureiro, Torbjørn Cunis, Walter Fichter
arxiv-2504-01851.description: Abstract Trajectory prediction of aerial vehicles is a key requirement in applications ranging from missile guidance to UAV collision avoidance. While most prediction methods assume deterministic target motion, real-world targets often exhibit stochastic behaviors such as evasive maneuvers or random gliding patterns.

arxiv-2509-24802.title: TACO-Net: Topological Signatures Triumph in 3D Object Classification
arxiv-2509-24802.creator: Anirban Ghosh, Ayan Dutta
arxiv-2509-24802.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anirban Ghosh, Ayan Dutta. 3D object classification is a crucial problem due to its significant practical relevance in many fields, including computer vision, robotics, and autonomous driving. Although deep learning methods applied to point clouds sampled on CAD models of the objects and/or captured by LiDAR or RGBD cameras have achieved remarkable success in recent years, achieving high classification accuracy remains a challenging problem due to the unordered point clouds and their irregularity and noise.

pmc-11293744.title: Comparative analysis of the liver transcriptome in the red-eared slider (Trachemys scripta elegans) post exposure to noise
pmc-11293744.creator: Guangwei Ma, Ziye Zuo, Handong Li, Xiaofei Zhai, Tongliang Wang, Jichao Wang
pmc-11293744.description: Exposure to noise can cause non-auditory health problems and has been widely studied in mammals such as rats and rabbits. However, the non-auditory effects of noise exposure on reptiles (such as red-eared sliders) remain unclear. In this study, we determined the noise exposure-induced transcriptomic changes in the liver of red-eared slider (Trachemys scripta elegans) using Illumina Novaseq6000 sequencing technology.

pmc-11550722.title: Revealing SARS-CoV-2 Mpro mutation cold and hot spots: Dynamic residue network analysis meets machine learning
pmc-11550722.creator: Victor Barozi, Shrestha Chakraborty, Shaylyn Govender, Emily Morgan, Rabelani Ramahala, Stephen C Graham, Nigel T Bishop, Özlem Tastan Bishop
pmc-11550722.description: Deciphering the effect of evolutionary mutations of viruses and predicting future mutations is crucial for designing long-lasting and effective drugs. While understanding the impact of current mutations on protein drug targets is feasible, predicting future mutations due to natural evolution of viruses and environmental pressures remains challenging.

pmc-13073760.title: Mesenchymal Tissue-Driven Gene Programs Identify EMP3 as a Key Biomarker of Aggressiveness in Undifferentiated Sarcomas
pmc-13073760.creator: Eun-Young Lee, Ahyoung Cho, Seog Yun Park, June Hyuk Kim, Hyun Guy Kang, Jong Woong Park, Jae Hyang Lim, Joonha Kwon, Hye Jin You
pmc-13073760.description: Undifferentiated sarcomas (USs), including undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (UPS), are aggressive mesenchymal malignancies with limited molecular biomarkers for prognostic assessment and therapeutic stratification. Expression-based markers may provide insight into tumor aggressiveness and clinical outcomes. Here, we performed integrative transcriptomic and spatial analyses to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). By comparing normal tissues with sarcoma tumors and sarcoma tumors with cell lines.

pmc-13385658.title: Number of Sprint Repetitions in a Sprint Interval Training Session Does Not Moderate Improvements in V̇O2max With Training: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13385658.creator: M. Hutchinson, D. J. Kinghorn, E. C. R. Hall, R. S. Metcalfe, D. R. Paval, I. J. Gallagher, N. B. J. Vollaard
pmc-13385658.description: Sprint interval training (SIT) is promoted as a time‐efficient method for improving maximal aerobic capacity (V̇O2max); however, the “classic” protocol (4–6 × 30‐s all‐out sprints) is less time‐efficient than claimed, may be poorly tolerated, and is expected to lead to low adherence.
